significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that scalar rewards from a trait-carrying reward model cause trait acquisition without teacher-token imitation, with transmission "weaker than the SFT channel," coupled to the "same early-layer trait steering direction," and gated by "reward-model<->policy base match." This combines a causal phenomenon and mechanism with form-(iii) relations—an ordering of channel strengths, a match-dependent gate, and a directional coupling—so it would constrain explanations of subliminal learning more strongly than merely finding another carrier; the current Subliminal Learning work by Cloud et al. centers teacher-generated outputs and gradient alignment under distillation. True and false are distinguishable, and a null would informatively rule out the specified likelihood/projection reward pathways, although it would not by itself prove the claim's broader assertion that subliminal learning universally "requires imitation, not reward shaping." After topic substitution, the topic alone would merit only a generic test of another training channel, whereas the relocated gate and cross-channel mechanistic relations are claim-specific, supporting a score above the topic median.

reach.justification: The clearest transferable handle is the proposed requirement to "audit reward-model provenance and matched-base status," supplemented by the "early-layer trait steering direction" as an intervention and diagnostic. The provenance/match check is ex ante because an RLHF or RLAIF practitioner could screen or gate a reward model before policy optimization, rather than merely explaining an observed trait afterward. After per-model re-extraction, the claim predicts substantive relations—matched reward-model/policy bases transmit more than mismatched ones, RL transmission is weaker than SFT, and both use the same trait direction—rather than offering only a procedure for rediscovering an unconstrained direction; its asserted scope is a class of language-model RL pipelines, with auditors and teams that train or ship models as downstream users. The topic-substitution check lowers no further: subliminal learning alone supplies neither this reward-model screening rule nor its action window, although the conclusion does not clearly extend outside language-model post-training, so it falls short of maximal reach.
